comparison: Both evaluate claims about Ca²⁺ entry not being affected by SERCA downregulation (C99-C102, C171). OpenEval finds these claims SUPPORTED by experimental data in Figure 4D. Peer reviewer also accepts these findings as evidence against store-operated calcium entry mechanisms in T. gondii.

Both address membrane contact sites between ER and other organelles (C138-C144, C178). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by EM data in Figure 6. Peer reviewer accepts the morphological evidence that contacts exist but editor notes uncertainty about whether these contacts are the mechanism for Ca²⁺ transfer versus other mechanisms.

Both evaluate claims about multiple Ca²⁺ stores and their functional links (C103-C108, C167-C170). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by experimental data. Peer reviewer accepts findings about Zaprinast and GPN targeting overlapping stores as supporting evidence for multiple intracellular Ca²⁺ stores.

Both evaluate the conditional knockout characterization (C84-C94, C157, C200, C203-C205). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by Figure 3 data showing essential role of TgSERCA. Peer reviewer does not challenge these phenotypic findings and accepts the data demonstrating TgSERCA's essential role in parasite biology.

Both address TG pre-treatment effects and ER-to-acidic store Ca²⁺ transfer (C56-C60, C105-C110, C127-C128, C132-C133, C166, C179-C180). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED. Peer reviewer expresses UNCERTAINTY, noting that TG-induced cytoplasmic Ca²⁺ rise could load acidic stores, questioning whether data definitively show direct ER-to-acidic store transfer versus cytosol-mediated transfer.

Both evaluate claims about Ca²⁺ pre-exposure enhancing organellar Ca²⁺ release capacity and ER-mediated redistribution (C47, C54-C55, C58, C63, C148, C150-C151, C165-C166, C190-C192, C206). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by Figure 1D-G data. Peer reviewer agrees, stating data support model where ER Ca²⁺ maintains Ca²⁺ levels in other organelles under physiological conditions.

Both address mitochondrial Ca²⁺ uptake from ER and acidic stores through membrane contact sites (C129-C133, C174-C175, C193). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by experimental data. Peer reviewer/editor express UNCERTAINTY about whether inter-organellar Ca²⁺ transport occurs via ER-mitochondria membrane contact sites or other mechanisms, though mitochondrial uptake data are not explicitly challenged.

Both evaluate the Mag-Fluo-4 assay validation and SERCA activity measurements (C64-C65, C80-C82, C145-C147, C158-C161). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by Figure 2 data. Peer reviewer accepts these findings, with editor stating study provides 'compelling evidence' using 'advanced imaging techniques' and data in Figures 2 and 4 are not questioned.

Both evaluate the central model of ER coordinating Ca²⁺ dynamics (C148-C149, C181, C199, C208). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED as main contribution of study. Peer reviewer agrees, describing it as 'important study' showing ER plays major role in regulating Ca²⁺ levels in cytosol and other organelles, with data supporting model where ER Ca²⁺ is mobilized for signaling and homeostasis.

Both evaluate differential effects of SERCA inhibitors on cytosolic Ca²⁺ (C44-C46, C78-C79, C162-C164). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by Figure 1B-C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-C. Peer reviewer does not challenge these findings comparing CPA and TG effects.

Both address validation of methods and differential effects of CPA and TG (C162-C164). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by experimental data and citations. Peer reviewer accepts these findings without challenge.

Both evaluate identity of acidic Ca²⁺ stores and their relationship with ER (C167-C170). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with some inference about GPN's primary target. Peer reviewer accepts findings about overlapping stores targeted by Zaprinast and GPN.

Both address ER Ca²⁺ dynamics and SERCA function (C63-C65, C80-C82). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by experimental data. Peer reviewer accepts findings as part of compelling evidence for SERCA's role in regulating organellar calcium levels.

Both evaluate ER contribution to filling acidic stores (C109-C110, C127-C128, C132-C133, C166, C179-C180). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED as key finding. Peer reviewer expresses UNCERTAINTY about mechanism, questioning whether transfer is direct or cytosol-mediated.

Both address Ca²⁺ transfer from acidic stores to mitochondrion (C127-C128, C132-C133, C166, C179-C180). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by Figure 5I-K. Peer reviewer expresses UNCERTAINTY about the mechanism of inter-organellar transfer.

Both evaluate differential effects on egress depending on trigger (C89-C92, C203-C205). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by Figure 3H. Peer reviewer accepts phenotypic findings from conditional knockout without challenge.

Both summarize essential role of TgSERCA in lytic cycle (C93-C94, C157, C200, C203-C205). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by experimental data. Peer reviewer accepts these findings demonstrating TgSERCA's essential role.

Both address SERCA activity maintaining Ca²⁺ balance across organelles (C150-C151, C165-C166, C190-C192). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by i△TgSERCA mutant data. Peer reviewer agrees with model where ER Ca²⁺ maintains levels in other organelles under physiological conditions.

Both evaluate Ca²⁺ transfer through ER-mitochondria MCSs (C174-C178, C193). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by experimental data and structural observations. Peer reviewer/editor express UNCERTAINTY about whether MCSs are the mechanism versus other pathways.

Both summarize inter-organellar Ca²⁺ transfer findings (C190-C192, C206). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED as strong evidence for proposed model. Peer reviewer agrees, finding data supportive of ER maintaining Ca²⁺ levels in other organelles.

Both evaluate main conclusions about ER's central role in Ca²⁺ dynamics (C206-C208). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED as comprehensive model. Peer reviewer agrees, describing study as important and supporting the overall model.
Both address Ca²⁺ transfer from acidic stores extending the inter-organelle model (C179-C181). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED. Peer reviewer expresses UNCERTAINTY about mechanism of transfer.

Both evaluate CPA effects in permeabilized versus intact parasites (C78-C79, C162-C164). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with some speculation about CPA reversibility. Peer reviewer accepts findings without challenge.

Both address TgSERCA properties and essential role (C158-C161). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by citations and experimental data. Peer reviewer accepts findings as part of compelling evidence for SERCA's role.
Both evaluate essential role of ER Ca²⁺ stores in egress (C200, C203-C205). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by experimental data. Peer reviewer accepts phenotypic findings without challenge.
Both address mitochondrial morphology changes (C134, C138-C144, C178). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by Figure 6A-B. Peer reviewer accepts morphological data showing contacts exist.

Both summarize membrane contact sites findings (C143-C144, C178). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED as structural basis for Ca²⁺ transfer. Peer reviewer accepts morphological evidence but editor notes uncertainty about functional mechanism.
Both address ER coordinating Ca²⁺ signaling for parasite functions (C199, C208). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by i△TgSERCA data. Peer reviewer agrees with overall model of ER's central role.
